quick.summary: Why developers reject finished designs, and when to show your work.
quick.takeaway: Share messy sketches early. Find out what is hard to build in week one.

beats.line: I made a prototype for a month. The developer killed it. Why?
You built a house before asking the builder if the pipes fit.
I wanted it perfect before I showed it.
Secret means risky. The fix is called early alignment.
Can I just say talk to them early?
Yes. Share your messy sketches. Ask what is hard to build.
But they might reject my favorite idea.
Better to know in week one than week four.
So I show them the rough ideas next Tuesday.
They will love being part of the plan.

quiz.question: When is the best time to show your work to a developer?
options: While the sketches are still rough and messy.
After you finish all the final pixels.
Only after the product manager approves it.
Right before the final launch date.
quiz.explanation: Showing messy work early lets you find out what is hard to build before you waste time.

quiz.question: Keeping your design secret until it is perfect reduces risk.
quiz.explanation: Secret means risky. Getting early feedback from other teams prevents major issues later.
